title: Bidirectional provenance attribution of chatbot text in writing and programming logs (FLoRA, RelianceScope): code, analysis log, benchmark, statistics
description: Version 1.25.0. Code, a dated analysis log and statistics files for a study of verbatim uptake of chatbot text in students' graded project proposals (FLoRA Open Data IPS, 275 students). v1.1.0 added log entry R1: time-aware echo correction, third-source filter, clock check from chat-box keystrokes, validation against logged paste events, and extended analyses of grades and detection. v1.2.0 adds log entry R2: three open zero-shot AI-text detectors (log-likelihood, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars on Qwen2.5 models) evaluated against logged provenance at paragraph level, by first language, and sensitivity of the third-source threshold. All analyses are exploratory. No third-party data are redistributed. v1.3.0 adds log entry R3: attribution of each token of the submitted artefact to five provenance classes (chatbot-first, echo, shared source, typed, untraced insertion), applied to FLoRA and to the RelianceScope programming dataset with validation against human response-use codes and an unaided post-test; FLoRA detector reanalysis on typed vs untraced text (post hoc). Third-party data are not redistributed. v1.4.0 adds log entry R4: entry mode by edit size, validation of typed and untraced classes against logged pastes, chance baseline and conservative bounds for chatbot-first code, length-controlled validation against human codes, and a censored model of the post-test. v1.4.1 records the RelianceScope authors' permission to use the dataset with citation; no analyses changed. v1.5.0 adds log entry R5: within-document moves in the untraced class, token-level projection, clock distribution, segment-local entry rule, origin of echo text, timing baseline by class, code-aware tokenisation for the programming data, robustness of the grade model (multiple imputation, censoring, transformations, class shares) and of the post-test models (chance-corrected and reference-excluded uptake, task progress), detector thresholds, and a size-matched and semantic paraphrase check. v1.6.0 adds log entry R6, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: attribution with degraded logs (dialogue only, thinned editor snapshots), effect of every parameter choice on the main quantities, chance baseline by n-gram length, descriptive subdivision of the untraced class, origin of logged pastes, minimum detectable effects and simulated power of the outcome models, and a self-contained end-to-end demonstration on synthetic logs (demo/). No measure or class definition changed. v1.7.0 adds log entry R7, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: comparison of students with and without logged paste events, agreement of segment uptake with each human response-use code, a diagram of the routes by which text reaches the editor, and the class figure recomputed with the edit-size entry rule. No measure or class definition changed. v1.8.0 adds log entry R8, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: sensitivity of the grade analysis to misclassification of untraced text, equivalence tests, order of the echo and shared-source rules, agreement with retyped code, a label-noise ceiling for the human codes, a comparison with the LLM classifiers released with RelianceScope, post-test models with pre-activity covariates, numerical-Hessian standard errors for the censored models, and token-level five-class labels produced by the attribution of the 275 FLoRA proposals (CC BY 4.0). No measure or class definition changed. v1.9.0 renames the analysis files from PREREG_* to ANALYSIS_LOG_* (file names cited inside them updated, content otherwise unchanged; the entries record decisions made as the analysis proceeded and are not pre-registrations) and adds log entry R9: accuracy against simulated logs with known routes under clock offsets, snapshot thinning and paraphrase; an audit of sampled passages against keystrokes and chatbot-panel selections that the attribution does not use; echo split by entry mode and route; run time; thinning by class; entry threshold and paste window; a token-level entry variant added after the audit result for typed text; and a decomposition of the chance baseline for code. The primary measure is unchanged. v1.10.0 adds log entry R10, committed before its analyses ran: a benchmark with planted provenance fitted to the FLoRA logs, with per-class confusion, precision and recall and student-level error of U* under several snapshot resolutions; winnowing (MOSS-style) and greedy string tiling (JPlag-style) baselines on the benchmark and on both datasets; an online version of the attribution with agreement, latency per snapshot and memory; attribution of intermediate snapshots and a parameter table for RelianceScope; a label-noise ceiling over a range of error rates; student-level intervals for the FLoRA paste checks. The primary measure is unchanged. v1.10.1 adds the R10 addendum counting conflicts between the ordered rules and relabels Figures 1, 2 and 4 with the four evidential classes and the unresolved outcome (X); no result changed. v1.11.0 adds log entry R11, committed before its analyses ran: empirical checks of the stated properties of the rules (soundness of the chatbot-first class, monotonicity of the online version, determinism); seven benchmark routes outside the specification of the rules (in-place editing of pasted replies, interleaved pasting and typing, regenerated replies, streaming replies, undo and redo); 50 random route mixes and 20 seeds with bootstrap intervals; earliest-plausible (WikiWho-style), paste-log and small-LLM baselines; risk-coverage analysis with the unresolved outcome as abstention; and FLoRA analyses of unresolved pastes, the shared-source rule, clock direction and audit clustering. The token-level entry rule becomes the primary rule for the typed/unresolved split; the chatbot-first, echo and shared-source classes and uptake are unchanged. Token-level and student-level FLoRA labels are re-exported. v1.12.0 adds log entry R12, written after its analyses had run: risk-coverage analysis with a stated confidence for every baseline and with abstention by entry size attached to earliest-plausible, dialogue-only and overlap baselines; the online version holds labels for delta seconds after entry so that it matches the offline rule when delta > 0; FLoRA unresolved tokens absent from the last snapshot, working span and timing, distribution of uptake, naive overlap at n = 5 and 12, paste comparisons with students as clusters, chatbot-panel selection by class; RelianceScope class shares under the token entry rule. No measure, class definition or parameter value changed. v1.13.0 adds log entry R13, written after its analyses ran: the decision list applied as written when delta > 0 (offline R2 with delta, online R1 for shared-source labels), sources of the remaining risk-coverage difference by route, FLoRA unresolved text in the first snapshot, panel selections for the token-rule audit sample and overlap of each class with English Wikipedia; no result with delta = 0 changed. v1.14.0 adds log entry R14, written after its analyses ran: risk-coverage difference with routes left out together, snapshots thinned to 300 s with the current code and the reading-highlight route across resolutions; nothing changed. v1.14.0 updated the metadata for the submission to Information Processing & Management; no analysis code changed. v1.15.0 adds log entry R15, written after its analyses ran in response to an internal review: benchmark routes on which the definitions of the typed and unresolved classes and the conditions that assign them diverge (outside text retyped, chunked or mixed with chatbot text), routes that violate the assumption that every outside source copied verbatim by the chatbot is a shared source, selective risk in the standard form, baselines with tolerant n-gram matching and with retrieval of reply windows by sentence embeddings, a stepwise decomposition of the FLoRA naive-overlap estimate with paired intervals and the verbatim overlap of replies to near-identical prompts; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.16.0 adds log entry R16, written after a second internal review and run after a test on small sets: a reporting partition of the unresolved class into subtypes by the evidence about entry, operating points for audit and screening, a grid over n, tau and delta, embedding thresholds tuned on separate simulated students with student-bootstrap intervals for the tolerant baselines, and an evidence-fusion classifier (gradient-boosted trees and logistic regression over 25 evidence features) trained on separate simulated students, tested on routes it had and had not seen, calibrated, and applied to the FLoRA logs; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.17.0 adds log entry R17, written after a third internal review and run after a test on small sets: risk-coverage in the standard form for every baseline with paired intervals by route, the assumption-A3 set decomposed, a hyperparameter search for the evidence-fusion classifier and its application to FLoRA, the benchmark rebuilt with outside text from two further sources (unresolved FLoRA runs without subtype evidence; arXiv abstracts), an LLM baseline (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, local), the echo class by route and entry size with bounds on the share of writers at or above half, a new keystroke audit of typed and unresolved passages independent of the sample that selected the entry rule, a keystroke census of echo, sources of large-entry echo, the peer threshold as a share of the cohort, chance coverage for n = 5 to 12, and the subtypes of the unresolved class without embedding flags; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.18.0 adds log entry R18, written in response to a review of the fourth version and run after a test on small sets: the timing of logged replies in FLoRA (latency against reply length; reply 8-grams that reached the editor before the logged reply time), the attribution with clock tolerance up to +120 s, snapshot transitions by inserted tokens with their keystroke support, the shared-source rule without the peer criterion for the student's own chatbot text, 2,000 paired resamples for the risk-coverage difference with earliest plausible attribution, student-bootstrap intervals for every evidence-fusion classifier, and a worked-example figure on the synthetic demo logs; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.19.0 adds log entry R19, written in response to a second review: writer text from an independent corpus in the benchmark, a decision-cost comparison of every method, shares of students at 25%, 50% and 75% under alternative counts, the entry threshold and the entry size of the final tokens, and editor-log completeness as effect sizes; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.20.0 adds log entry R20, written in response to comments on the fifth version and run after a test on small sets: the assumption-A3 set at three route weights, structural editing of chatbot text, route mixes far from FLoRA, selective risk of the evidence-fusion classifiers, earliest plausible attribution (n-gram and WikiWho) on the FLoRA logs, the echo class split by entry after the reply, and coincidence with replies to similar prompts; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.21.0 adds log entry R21, written in response to the same comments for the seventh version and run after a test on small sets: chatbot text revised by an open language model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, local) in the benchmark, an open model's replies (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, local) to the writers' own prompts compared verbatim with each provenance class, and a figure of four labelled FLoRA proposals chosen by percentile of the chatbot-first share; every generated text is released; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.22.0 adds log entry R22: the frozen attribution applied, unchanged, to the public NIRVANA dataset (77 students, GPT-3.5-turbo), whose platform logged copies from ChatGPT, with the plan committed and pushed before the full run; post hoc analyses of that application, tolerant matching on model-revised chatbot text, and the FLoRA post-task survey answers that name outside chatbots. v1.23.0 adds log entry R23, written after its analyses ran: the FLoRA share of chatbot text reported as a range identified under nested logging and behavioural assumptions, a data-driven rule for the entry threshold, a census of chatbot-first runs against keystrokes, chatbot-panel selections and logged pastes, and, from the stored outputs of R22 because the NIRVANA project was no longer publicly accessible, NIRVANA agreement by stratum of entry, naive overlap scored on the copy signal and a bound on coincidence; nothing in the attribution changed. v1.24.0 adds log entry R24: the frozen attribution applied to CoAuthor (1,445 writing sessions with GPT-3 suggestions), whose platform logged every accepted suggestion, with the plan pushed before the full run; CoAuthor replaces NIRVANA as the hold-out set because the NIRVANA project stopped being publicly accessible. v1.25.0 adds log entry R25: on CoAuthor, a test of the identified range against the platform's record of inserted model text, and the subtypes of the unresolved class. v1.25.0 is the version that produced every result reported in the article 'What dialogue and editor logs can establish about chatbot text in student writing: token-level provenance with direction and abstention' (submitted to Information Processing & Management).
